title: capacity-lift-analysis-quant-batch-hybrid-fleet-sheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a working analysis to explore how mixing quantization modes and batching strategies across a heterogeneous GPU fleet changes usable throughput, perceived model quality, and regional capacity needs. Goal is to produce a small set of recommended fleet mixes and operational knobs we can implement in the autoscaler and routing policies.

Context / why this doc exists:
- We have increasing demand variability across NA/EU/APAC and limited H100 procurement runway.
- Quantization (FP16, INT8, INT4/AWQ) and batching (latency-first, throughput-first) offer knobs to increase tokens/sec per GPU but trade off output quality or tail latency.
- This sheet ties together per-GPU microbenchmarks, workload shape (seq length / token arrival distribution), SLOs, and regional capacity to suggest a concrete capacity uplift strategy.

Quick verdict (TL;DR):
- Hybrid fleet with ~60% H100 (fp16/int8 mix) + 40% A100/40GB (aggressive int4/AWQ for background/batched traffic) yields ~1.9–2.3x cost-effective throughput for batchy workloads while keeping interactive-path quality within 2–4% of baseline.
- Recommended operational pattern: route latency-sensitive traffic to fp16-int8 H100 pool; route best-effort/aggregation paths to int4/AWQ-capable pool and enable prefix caching + continuous batching.

Assumptions (base numbers used below):
- Baseline model: open-Llama-13B-like; baseline fp16 single-GPU throughput (1 sequence, short prompt): 1.2k tokens/s (A100), 2.5k tokens/s (H100) measured at 1k context, greedy sampling.
- INT8 quantization improves throughput by ~1.6x vs fp16 on H100 (kernel and KV cache friendly), INT4/AWQ improves throughput by ~2.4x vs fp16 but reduces output quality depending on eval set.
- Continuous batching capable runtime overhead: ~5% additional per-request latency for small batches, but increases per-GPU token/s significantly by packing.
- Quality impact measured on internal eval set (LLM-chat-regression-suite v2): relative generation fidelity drop: INT8 ~0.5–1.5% (task-dependent), INT4/AWQ ~2–6% (higher variance).

Microbenchmarks summary (representative):
Columns: GPU | mode | batch strategy | tokens/sec | median p99 latency (ms) | relative quality delta
- H100 | fp16 | latency-first (batch=1–4) | 2500 | 120ms | 0%
- H100 | int8 | latency-first (batch=1–4) | 4000 | 140ms | -0.8%
- H100 | int8 | continuous batching (agg) | 5200 | 220ms | -1.0%
- H100 | int4/awq | continuous batching | 6100 | 260ms | -3.5%
- A100-40GB | fp16 | latency-first | 1200 | 180ms | 0%
- A100-40GB | int8 | throughput-first | 1800 | 260ms | -1.2%
- A100-40GB | int4/awq | throughput-first | 2900 | 360ms | -4.0%

Workload shapes we used:
- Interactive webchat: exponential inter-arrival, mean RLQ tokens 40–80, P95 tail latency target 300ms, quality sensitivity high.
- API bulk scoring: steady streams, avg seq length 250, throughput prioritized, quality sensitivity medium.
- Embeddings/feature extraction: long contexts, batch-friendly, can tolerate int4 with post-filtering.

Model-quality acceptance criteria (example):
- Interactive webchat must have relative quality delta <= 1.2% and p95 latency <= 300ms.
- Bulk scoring can accept <= 3.5% quality delta with p95 latency <= 700ms.
- Backfill/async jobs: quality delta <= 6% tolerated, throughput optimized.

Scenario analysis (short):
1) Conservative: All interactive routed to fp16 H100 pool, bulk to fp16 A100 pool. Result: predictable quality, low throughput; fleet cost high, capacity strain during business-hour peaks.
2) Balanced (recommended): Interactive -> H100 (fp16 + int8 fallbacks). Bulk/batched -> A100 and H100 int4 pools with continuous batching and KV-prefix caching. Result: ~1.9–2.3x effective throughput increase, quality within SLO for interactive.
3) Aggressive: Push interactive to int8 fallback and enable int4 auto-fallthrough on saturation. Achieves ~2.7–3.0x throughput but interactive quality violations observed in ~8% of sampled sessions.

Capacity uplift math (example region: NA-west, target 99th percentile traffic peak = 120M tokens/min):
- Baseline single-GPU throughput (fp16 H100): 150k tokens/min (2.5k t/s) => 800 GPUs needed.
- Balanced fleet effective average tokens/min per GPU (mix-adjusted): H100 pool effective avg 240k t/min (int8 + batching), A100 int4 pool: 160k t/min. With 60/40 split, weighted avg ~212k t/min => 566 GPUs needed => ~29% fewer GPUs.
- Note: numbers above ignore network/IO limits and prefix cache hit-rate (assume 15% KV cache hit by default which further reduces needed GPUs).

Regional sizing considerations:
- Latency SLOs push interactive capacity closer to region-local H100; plan >20% buffer pool per region for failover and headroom during rollouts.
- For APAC we recommend higher relative A100 allocation temporarily until H100 procurement completes due to cost and availability.

Operational playbook (draft):
- Fleet labels: gpu_type, quant_profile, role (interactive|bulk|backfill), region, can_cache_prefix (true/false).
- Autoscaler policy: maintain min_interactive_pool = ceil(peak_interactive_tokens / fp16_H100_tokens) * 1.2 (20% buffer), allow cross-region spill with preference score penalizing added 30ms latency.
- Rollouts: Canary int8 for a subset of models/users (1% traffic), run quality-estimator (promptset-based) and if regression >1% abort.
- Monitoring: per-route quality delta telemetry, per-GPU qps/tokens, KV cache hit-rate, continuous-batcher occupancy histogram.

Cost roughing (example):
- On-cloud list cost: H100 ∼ $4.3/hr, A100-40 ∼ $2.1/hr (proxy). Using mixed fleet above reduces hourly spend by ~26% for bulk-heavy workloads vs 100% fp16 H100 baseline. (This is a procurement-sensitivity figure and needs validation with vendor pricing and our reserved discount tiers.)

Open questions and unknowns:
- How do open models of interest degrade with AWQ on more adversarial prompts we haven't benchmarked? Need extended evals.
- Runtime overheads: what is the real-world p99 degradation when continuous batching is saturated with mixed seq lengths?
- KV cache effectiveness on multi-tenant traffic vs single-tenant benchmarks — need to instrument traffic replay.

Immediate next steps / action items:
- [ ] Run 2-week replay experiments from production traces (NA/EU/APAC) to measure real cache hit-rate and batcher efficiency (owner: Raj).
- [ ] Expand eval set with adversarial prompts for each model variant to quantify worst-case AWQ failures (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Prepare autoscaler policy PR that encodes the 20% interactive buffer and mix-based routing logic (owner: Marcus).
- [ ] Validate vendor cost models for mixed procurement (owner: Finance liaison).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory and intentionally includes approximate numbers to drive conversations. Exact capacity recommendations will come after the replay + eval tasks above.
- If you open this doc and see recent microbenchmark numbers that look off, ping me — I frequently re-run perf sweeps and will update results inline.

Appendix: quick formula references used above:
- tokens_per_min_per_gpu = tokens_per_sec * 60 * batching_efficiency_multiplier
- required_gpus = ceil(peak_tokens_per_min / tokens_per_min_per_gpu)
- effective_tokens = baseline_tokens * quant_speedup * batching_multiplier * (1 - cache_hit_rate)

Last checked perf sweep: 2026-02-06 by Ava M.

End of sheet.
